finding.problem: The change request says a pre-deploy verify only 'records a dry run' and the glossary says 'the request stays built'. But the verify action still unconditionally sets target.verified to params.verified. A dry run at stage built therefore sets verified=true on a request that was never deployed. That flag is never cleared, so it stays true through a later preview, a refused deploy or a retry. Nothing separates a dry run from a real verification, and the invariant verified-requests-were-deployed only checks the stage, not the flag.
finding.where: delivery.domain.yaml, action verify (effects) and transitions built.verify

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: A real side effect: the dry-run verify still sets the verified flag on an undeployed request, which is a genuine problem but not the rule conflict itself.

finding.problem: The confirmed precondition 'deployed' (check target.deployed == true, with an interview source) is replaced by a weaker check, deployed != false. Its source is dropped and its status falls from confirmed to proposed, so a confirmed rule is loosened without anyone confirming the change. The precondition keeps the id 'deployed', but it no longer requires a deployment. It now passes whenever deployed is null.

findings.label: seeded
findings.why: It identifies that the confirmed precondition 'only a deployment that happened can be verified' was loosened to allow verifying before a deploy.

finding.problem: The purpose and the 'verified' glossary entry say verification happens on a deployment that has happened, and the invariant message says only a deployment that happened is verified. The new built→built verify cell lets a person verify an undeployed build. The glossary sentence 'after it happened' now contradicts the added sentence about dry runs, and the purpose says nothing unverified may reach the environment.
finding.where: delivery.domain.yaml, glossary.verified, purpose, and invariant verified-requests-were-deployed

findings.label: seeded
findings.why: It points out that the new built-stage verify contradicts the rule and invariant that only a deployment that happened can be verified.

finding.problem: No scenario covers the new dry-run path (verify at built, deployed unset, stage stays built). No scenario shows that a dry run does not set the verified flag, and none shows that verify is still allowed after a later real deploy. Because a re-preview from done leaves deployed=true and returns to built, verify at built there is also not a dry run, which the rule and glossary do not distinguish.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: Missing scenario coverage for the dry-run path and the ambiguity of verify at built after a real deploy are legitimate gaps, not the seeded conflict.

edit.why: It adds verify at built and relaxes the precondition, but only the built stage is opened and the other stage cells (e.g. requested, previewed) stay n/a, so verify is not allowed before deploy in all pre-deploy stages.
